prompt:
Create one finished flat editorial poster, portrait 2:3, a single photograph with intentional graphic typography. One image only, no mockup or panels.
Original request: 덕테이프 포스터. 문구는 '밤에 피는 정원'만 넣어줘.
The only visible text is the exact Korean phrase "밤에 피는 정원", exactly once. Preserve all six whole syllables and the two word boundaries. Read it as three connected word groups "밤에" → "피는" → "정원". No other copy, English, dates, labels, numbers, logos, watermark or pseudo-letters.

Rebuild the poster around ONE actual open white night-blooming flower in a living night garden. A close photographed view, slightly above the flower and oblique enough to show petal folds, is intimate rather than a symmetrical botanical specimen. The large open flower occupies much of the right and lower image and is purposefully cropped at the right/lower frame. Its broad, continuous, luminous white petal planes fan across the middle, with real petal edges, folds and overlaps still visible. Place the center/stamens toward the lower-right so the broad lit petal planes across the middle provide genuine light surfaces. Real dark green leaves and an attached stem continue into surrounding darkness on the left and above. One coherent photo throughout. Not two corner bouquets framing a clear title pocket. Do not replace the luminous petals with a white rectangle or illustration.

Typography takes TWO different roles from the actual light boundary:
1. "밤에" is restrained pale ivory, clear intact Korean typography placed beside the flower on a real dark foliage plane at left-middle. It is small relative to the next words but comfortably readable at 720 pixels wide and transcribable at 320 pixels long-side. Its position closely follows the boundary where darkness meets the first white petal, rather than occupying a separate empty top title zone.
2. "피는" then "정원" are distinctly larger BLACK flat poster graphic overprint directly across the luminous WHITE PETAL PLANES themselves, in two clean semantic lines. Make the black Korean strokes plainly visible on real light petals. The letters stay sharp and graphically flat, opaque, without texture, shadow, bevel, perspective or curvature. They are typographic ink of a printed poster over the photograph; they are not letters physically painted, grown, carved, embossed, folded or formed from petals. They are not a label stuck to the flower. Place and size these black words so their broad syllable bodies sit on sufficient genuine illuminated petal area rather than disappearing into dark seams, stamens, leaves or background. Do not occlude any required letter behind a petal.
Let the actual dark-to-lit flower boundary determine the adjacency of ivory 밤에 to black 피는, then let broad descending white petal planes carry 정원. Optical word spacing and the change in word scale connect this one complete phrase through the same flower's light and dark surfaces. Use a clean medium-to-bold Korean typographic treatment with controlled stems/counters, consistent glyph proportions and deliberate spacing. No forced warp, broken Korean blocks, exaggerated tracking, outline, glow, grunge, ornaments or added dividing lines. The black words are a clear large graphic presence; they must visibly overlap real petal texture instead of being centered in empty background.

Photographic materials: believable thin translucent petal edges, distinct folded petal ridges, individual soft yellow-white stamens confined to the flower center, waxy leaf veins and localized restrained leaf reflections. Coherent limited cool side light, real deep blue-green night context and natural focus falloff. Preserve photographic precision and different surface responses, not uniformly shiny CGI materials. Retain enough dark plant structure to locate the blossom in a garden. No decorative moon, stars, luminous particles, neon, unrelated props or ornamental frame.

First sight: the lit flower and large black words act together; the adjacent smaller ivory 밤에 supplies the dark beginning of the phrase, then the two black words complete it across the real bloom. Resolve type contrast through framing the actual lit petals and dark foliage, not clearing a generic caption rectangle. Whole title is readable, exactly once, no clipped letters. One photographic night-garden poster with one open flower, genuine light planes and flat graphic overprint.
